newsitem.title: UK: Brit Airways drops despite top-end results.
newsitem.headline: Brit Airways drops despite top-end results.

text.p: British Airways Plc saw its shares indicated lower in line with the market on Monday, despite delivering record year profits which beat expectations.
Shares were indicated down 6 1/2 at 753 1/2 pence per share in pre-market trading despite pre-tax and pre-exceptional profits hitting a record 640 million stg versus 585 million the previous year.

Analysts had been pitching for profits of between 600 and 630 million stg. BA's dividend was also better than expected at 15.05 pence for the year after concensus predictions that it would be set at 15 pence per share. The record profits came despite a strong pound and a 20 percent rise in fuel costs.
Market players admitted that the results were impressive but said the shares had had a good run in recent weeks and investors were now taking the chance to cash in their spoils.
"They were very strong before the figures came out -- gaining around 10 percent in recent sessions," said one trader. " You could say, sometimes it is better to travel than to arrive."

One transport analyst at another investment house agreed BA's recent strength had fizzled out. "The results were at the top end of the range and BA has done extremely well. But after the last couple of weeks we have been recommending investors to take profits," he said.

British Airways' results included a 127 million stg charge related to restructuring. The airline group also announced a 94 million "birthday bonus" for its employees which included 10 free shares to celebrate the group's tenth anniversary since privatisation.
Sir Colin Marshall, BA chairman, said the coming year should see "continuing growth in demand for air travel" with the U.S. and UK economies looking robust.
He added that sterling's strength would have an adverse impact on profits this year but "this will partially be offset by lower fuel prices and further business efficiency improvements."
